# RTK - Rust Token Killer

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy (60-90% savings on dev operations)

## Meta Commands (always use rtk directly)

```bash
rtk gain              # Show token savings analytics
rtk gain --history    # Show command usage history with savings
rtk discover          # Analyze Claude Code history for missed opportunities
rtk proxy <cmd>       # Execute raw command without filtering (for debugging)
```

## Installation Verification

```bash
rtk --version         # Should show: rtk X.Y.Z
rtk gain              # Should work (not "command not found")
which rtk             # Verify correct binary
```

⚠️ **Name collision**: If `rtk gain` fails, you may have reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit) installed instead.

## Hook-Based Usage

All other commands are automatically rewritten by the Claude Code hook.
Example: `git status` → `rtk git status` (transparent, 0 tokens overhead)

Refer to CLAUDE.md for full command reference.

# Agent guide

Rules for AI agents working in this repo.

## Crates

| Crate | License | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callisto-model | MIT | none |
| callisto-manifests | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-graph | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests |
| callisto-cli | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph |
| callisto-fixtures | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) |

- `callisto-model` (MIT) must never depend on an FSL crate.
- Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml` after adding or moving a crate.

## Commands

- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
  - Never run cargo builds in parallel.
- Changesets: `callisto add --package callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic, written as the changelog entry: what the user sees now, no internal names or mechanism.
- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.

## Invariants

1. Safe Rust only: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
2. Manifest edits preserve format: `toml_edit` for TOML; JSON keeps key order and fingerprinted indentation. No regex or line edits.
3. File writes go through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. User-facing errors derive `miette::Diagnostic` with a code and a fix.
5. No emojis in docs or code.
6. No cargo features in shipped crates; behaviour is chosen at runtime (#143). The dev-only `callisto-model/test-util` feature is the exception.

## Fixing bugs

- Grep for structurally identical code (same algorithm, other file, ecosystem or mode). A sibling with the same defect is in scope now.
- N copies of one logic: unify to one implementation rather than patching each.
- A deliberately deferred sibling gets an explicit record: changeset note, tracked follow-up or code comment.
- A new shared helper migrates every call site in the same change, or the rest are tracked.

## Specs and plans

- Specs (`spec@1`) live in `docs/specs/`, one per area, current behavior only. Change the spec in the same PR as the behavior. No history, rationale or revision notes.
- This repo's release workflow has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate and only `execute` gets registry secrets (owner policy, enforced by `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`). Never add one.
- Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the matching `docs/architecture/` topic before changing behavior in an area.
- Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing release flow, Git access, publishing, distribution, platform packages or manifest writes. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR the owner accepts.
- Plans (`plan@1`) live in `docs/projects/`. Delete a plan once its work ships.
- Code never cites specs: no spec IDs, criterion IDs, section numbers or track names in comments, test names or messages. Describe the behavior instead.
- A requirement the owner didn't state is a judgment call. Get owner confirmation before it gates anything.

## Writing

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown or PR bodies: one line per paragraph.
- Code comments: one short line, only for a non-obvious why. Wrap at 120 columns (`rustfmt.toml`). No history ("used to", "previously"): git records it.
- No claude.ai session links in commits, PRs or files.

- [Post-0.10.2 Plan](project_post_0_10_2_plan.md) — Open work after the 0.10.2 release lives in docs/projects/NEXT-WORK.md (PR #201): 12 workstreams, parallel lanes, stacked PRs, owner decisions (D01 blocks MATURIN/OWNER).

- [Always Use Plugins](feedback_always_use_plugins.md) — Route PR/commit narration and audits through courier/ranger/etc. plugin agents by default, not freehand, even when I already have full context.
- [Terse Comments Only](feedback_terse_comments.md) — One short line max, only for non-obvious WHY; stop writing multi-line prose comments in code/config even though CLAUDE.md already says this.
- [Cargo Slowness Root Cause](project_cargo_slowness_target_pollution.md) — Hours-long builds were a polluted target/debug (1.7M .o files); wipe it, split-debuginfo=off, one invocation shape, no parallel builds; cold build is 31 s.
- [No Red-Green, Lean Tokens](feedback_no_red_green_lean_tokens.md) — User dropped red-green testing and wants lean token spend; no heavy agent gating loops; CLI product tag callisto@{version} is intentional.
- [PR #101 Hardening State](project_pr101_hardening_state.md) — 7 local unpushed commits fix the audited release-lifecycle defects; deferred structural work, unverified-on-GitHub items, and the git add -u lesson.
- [Never Hard-Wrap Prose](feedback_never_hard_wrap_prose.md) — PR descriptions and all Markdown: one line per paragraph, never manual line breaks.
- [Succinct Written Artifacts](feedback_succinct_written_artifacts.md) — Changesets, PR bodies, docs: short, plain, no AI slop or backstory.
- [No Session Links](feedback_no_session_links.md) — Never put claude.ai session URLs/Claude-Session trailers in commits or PRs; public repo, private sessions.
- [Verify Before Recommending](feedback_verify_before_recommending.md) — Check code, callers and sibling repos before presenting any recommendation; audit findings are leads, not conclusions.
- [No Thin ADRs](feedback_no_thin_adrs.md) — ADRs only for significant decisions, with rejected options, enforcement and revisit triggers; process rules aren't ADRs.
- [Budget: Lean Pipeline](feedback_budget_lean_pipeline.md) — weekly token budget; leanest pipeline that still catches bugs; no cleanup agents or rework the user has to review.
- [Use gh stack](feedback_use_gh_stack.md) — stacked PRs must be native GitHub stacks (gh stack link); plain chained PRs get no CI.
- [Agent Context Briefs](feedback_agent_context_briefs.md) — curated 2-4k token briefs, one agent per PR via SendMessage, small fixes directly; no forks of long sessions.

## Review: per-declaration Cargo edges (`DepLocator`)

I found no defect in the Cargo change itself. The one real defect is a Python sibling this change leaves behind. I read the code only: I did not compile, run tests or use git. Base is `wave1-base`, change is `wf_2ced9da6-4b8-2`. No FINDINGS.md exists, so nothing was skipped as already logged.

### Findings, ranked

**1. MEDIUM, sibling not fixed or recorded: Python still has the "first declaration is the reference" bug. Confirmed by reading, not a regression.**
- Location: `crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs`. Extras handling is at ~601-637, the `[project.dependencies]` loop at ~579-599, and `iter_dependencies` at ~459-557.
- The change passes `DepLocator::default()` for Python. AGENTS.md "Fixing bugs" puts a sibling with the same defect in scope now, or requires an explicit record. There is no changeset note, no comment and no follow-up.
- The Python extras writer still holds the design the Cargo change removed. A comment there says "the first declaration in table order is the one the graph sees; only declarations carrying the same constraint are rewritten with it". That comment is already wrong: the graph sees every declaration, because `iter_dependencies` emits one edge each.
- All those edges share one `RewriteKey` `(manifest, name, Some(kind), default)`. In the cascade's main pass, `out.rewrites.insert` lets the last stale edge's `to` win.
- Scenario A (extras):
  ```
  [project.optional-dependencies]
  a = ["b>=1.0"]
  c = ["b==1.0.0"]
  ```
  `b` goes to 1.1.0.
  - Edge 1 covers. Edge 2 does not, so the rewrite is `==1.1.0`.
  - The floor pass skips edge 1 because the key is already in `rewrite_attempted`.
  - The writer takes `>=1.0` as the reference and rewrites that line to `b==1.1.0`. It skips the stale `b==1.0.0`.
  - Result: the loose declaration becomes a pin and the stale pin stays.
- Scenario B (markers):
  ```
  [project] dependencies = ["b==1.0.0; python_version<'3.9'", "b==1.0.0; python_version>='3.9'"]
  ```
  Two edges share one key. The writer replaces the first match and `break`s. The second stays at `b==1.0.0`.
- The fix is to unify with the Cargo approach (a per-declaration locator, for example array index or extra name) rather than patch each copy.
- npm has no sibling. Its kinds map to distinct JSON objects and distinct keys.

**2. LOW-MEDIUM, public API breaks and a user-visible behaviour change are not recorded.**
- Breaking changes in published crates:
  - callisto-model: new `pub struct DepLocator`. `DependencyEntry` and `DepEdge` each gain a required pub field `locator`. Neither is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so any external struct literal breaks.
  - callisto-manifests: `Manifest::update_dependency_spec` has a new required parameter `at: &DepLocator`. The trait is not sealed, so external implementors and callers break.
  - callisto-graph: `cascade::RewriteKey` gains pub field `locator`. `RewriteKey` is re-exported at `callisto-graph/src/lib.rs:43`.
- Outside callers:
  - I checked every `DepEdge {`, `DependencyEntry {` and `RewriteKey {` literal in `crates/` with a script. All set `locator`.
  - There is no `impl Manifest` or `impl DependencyResolver` outside these crates. `callisto-fixtures`, `fuzz/` and `testing/` do not touch these types. The `DependencyResolver` trait signature is unchanged.
- `.changeset/` holds only the unrelated `clever-badgers-race.md` (`callisto-cli: patch`). `just check-api` runs `cargo semver-checks check-release`.
- The changeset rule applies too: the behaviour is user-visible. A target-table declaration that still covers the new version now gets its floor raised, and a stale target declaration now triggers a dependent bump.
- The spec criterion at `docs/specs/versioning.json:113` already says "every such spec ... raised", so no spec edit is needed.

**3. LOW, duplicate and indistinct diagnostics.**
- Edge construction (`walk.rs:769`) calls `resolve_native_with_fallback(..., diagnostics)` once per declaration. A cross-ecosystem or ambiguous name now warns once per declaration.
- Cascade `LeftAlone` warnings (`cascade.rs:281-284` and `482-484`) also repeat per declaration. They come from `rewrite_spec` (`cascade.rs:602`) with `package: None, path: None`, and the message carries only the spec text.
- Two target declarations with the same unrewritable range give two identical, untraceable warnings. Nothing dedupes diagnostics.
- Related: the CLI test input was changed from `>=0.1, <0.3` to `>=0.1.0, <0.3.0` (`cascade_scenarios_tests.rs`).
  - `round_trip` parses the `<` clause with `Version::parse` (SemVer, needs three components) and returns `None` on `<0.3`.
  - So a two-part upper bound in a target table now yields a `RangeNotRoundTrippable` warning at every release, where before it was silent. The test change avoids that path.
  - This limitation already existed for plain `[dependencies]`.

**4. LOW, tests that cannot catch the regression they name (checked against the old code).**
- `an_inherited_declaration_in_two_tables_writes_the_workspace_dependency_once` passes on old code. It asserts file text only, and a double write of the same value gives identical text. It would not fail if the locator leaked into the inherited key. An open-count or persist-count assertion is needed.
- `dev_and_build_declarations_are_rewritten_in_every_table` passes on old code. All four declarations are `=1.0.0`, so the old fingerprint matched them. It does exercise `at.section` taking precedence over `kind` for the optional-in-build case.
- `one_key_naming_different_crates_in_two_tables_rewrites_only_the_bumped_crate` passes on old code. It is a valid guard but not a regression test.
- The following do fail on old code: the first, second, third and fourth tests, the inherited-plus-target test, and the snapshot test.
- Missing cases:
  - a target-only inherited declaration;
  - an `optional = true` runtime declaration beside a target one;
  - a stale locator surfacing through `apply_version_plan`. Apply is not transactional across manifests, so earlier manifests stay written when a later step errors.
  - `DependencyNotFound` names neither the table nor the target (`cargo.rs:428`), so the user cannot see which declaration went stale.

**5. NIT.**
- `DepLocator.section: Option<DepKind>` allows `Peer` and `Optional`. `section_name` (`cargo.rs:487`) silently maps both to `dependencies`.
- The `DepLocator` doc and the `section` field doc are two lines each (AGENTS wants one short line).
- No emoji, unsafe code or spec IDs in the new code.
- `cargo.rs:98` ("previously") and `cargo.rs:796` ("no longer") are in the base, not introduced here.

### Probes that came back clean (confirmed by reading)

- **Duplicate edges between the same two packages.**
  - `toposort_with_edge_filter` (`toposort.rs:62-90`) increments `in_degree` once per edge and decrements once per `adj` entry. That is balanced, so ordering is unchanged and there are no false cycles.
  - Tarjan SCC (`cyclic_sccs`, `PublishEdgeFilter`) ignores multiplicity.
  - `link_publish_prerequisites` and `require_dependencies_selected` use sets or early returns. Duplicate edges of one kind already existed (runtime plus build).
  - `dependents_of` is used only by the cascade. Cascade severity is a max, `raise` is idempotent, and `iterations` counts package pops, not edges.
  - The reason shown in a bump (`raise`) is now the first stale declaration, which is correct.
  - There is no consumer in status, report or matrix. `snapshot.rs:71` dedupes through `BTreeMap<RewriteKey,_>` with `entry().or_insert_with`. Nothing else keys by `(name, kind)`.
- **Cascade key logic.**
  - `rewrite_attempted` and `out.rewrites` are keyed per declaration.
  - Inherited keys drop the locator (`cascade.rs:178`), so a workspace dependency named in several member tables or kinds gives one key and one root rewrite (`WriteStep::WorkspaceRoot`).
  - The root-as-member case routes inherited edges through `CargoWorkspaceDependency` and non-inherited ones through `Manifest`. `classify_manifest_writes` marks that path `excluded`. Mixed steps do a fresh load and persist each, so there is no stale overwrite. The `InvariantViolation` guard stays.
- **Writer (`cargo.rs:420-465`).**
  - It looks up exactly the declaration the locator names.
  - `[target.'cfg(unix)'...]` versus a bare key is the same normalized TOML key. A quoting mismatch is not possible, and duplicate spellings are a parse error.
  - Same key naming different crates is separate per locator. An `optional = true` declaration under dev or build now resolves via `at.section`. In the old code it hit `dependencies` and failed.
  - Peer is still rejected first.
  - A stale locator returns `DependencyNotFound` rather than skipping silently.
  - Comments and decor survive: `set_dependency_version` is unchanged, and the first test in `cargo_declaration_edges_test.rs` asserts the comments.
- **Borrow and compile shape.** The `not_found` closure and the split `self.document` borrow look valid for edition 2021. I could not verify by compiling.
